# Lanserhof (Tegernsee / Lans / Sylt — European medical-wellness resort)

URL: https://lanserhof.com/en/

## Type system
- Display/nav: `Fruitiger, arial, helvetica, sans-serif`, hero H1 at 52.8px/400,
  set in tight stacked uppercase ("LAN / SER / HOF") as the logo lockup itself
  — the wordmark is broken across three lines rather than run horizontally,
  reinforcing a slow, architectural read.
- H2 (section intros): same Fruitiger family, 36px/400, sentence case, e.g.
  "We embody the pinnacle of **excellence** in preventative health,
  regeneration, and optimisation" — a few words bolded mid-sentence for
  emphasis instead of a whole bold headline.
- Body: Fruitiger 14px/400, generous line-height, kept short (2–3 sentence
  paragraphs per block).
- No serif, no mono anywhere — a single humanist sans carries the entire
  identity, at very restrained sizes for a hero (most "hero" text on this
  page is smaller than a typical SaaS h1).

## Color system
- bg: near-white `#FFFFFF` and off-white `#F7F7F7`, alternating by section.
- text: dark slate `#2C2F38` / `#2B2E38` — never pure black.
- accent: powder blue `#96BDCD`, used sparingly (a small CTA pill, an award
  badge ring) — the only saturated colour on the page.
- Full-bleed photography (spa interiors, forest/lake landscapes, guests in
  robes) supplies all remaining colour; the UI chrome itself is almost
  achromatic.

## Layout & grid
- Full-bleed hero photograph with the stacked wordmark overlaid directly on
  the image, no scrim beyond natural photo contrast.
- Content below reverts to a comfortable ~1100px reading column with large
  asymmetric image/text pairings (image left, text right, alternating).
- Generous vertical whitespace between sections (multiple viewport-heights
  of breathing room) — pacing reads like a print magazine, not a
  conversion-optimized landing page.

## Sections (order observed)
1. Full-bleed hero photo, stacked wordmark, "Home of Health & Beauty"
   tagline, small booking-request card bottom-left
2. "Lanserhof Concept" — portrait photo + excellence/regeneration statement
3. "Medical Packages" — "Live better. For longer." claim + method description
4. "Our Locations" — single wide photo banner linking to property pages
5. "Our Awards" — row of small monochrome award/press logos
6. "Lanserhof Shop" — still-life product photography, home-retail upsell
7. "Our Health Guide" — editorial article cards (magazine-style, not blog
   teasers)
8. "Impressions from the resorts" — image carousel
9. Newsletter signup (dark textured background)
10. Instagram grid + dark footer

## Components/signature
- The stacked three-line wordmark used as both logo and hero headline —
  doubles as navigation anchor and brand mark.
- Mid-sentence bold emphasis inside otherwise regular-weight paragraphs,
  used repeatedly as the site's only typographic hierarchy trick within
  body copy.
- Awards row presented as small circular/shield badges, not a wall of press
  logos — reads more like a boutique hotel's accolades than a health
  company's clinical certifications.

## Motion/interactions
- Minimal — mostly static full-bleed imagery with a slow image carousel in
  the "Impressions" section; no dashboard, chart, or biomarker visualization
  anywhere on the homepage (medical content lives one click deeper, on
  "Medical Packages"/"Health Guide" pages).

## Biomarker/trust presentation
- No biomarker charts or scores on the homepage at all — trust is carried
  entirely by photography (real facilities, real guests), press/award
  logos, and prose describing the "Lanserhof Concept" (naturopathy +
  chronomedicine + modern medicine). This is a deliberate contrast to the
  DTC health-tech sites in this dataset: the luxury-resort cluster sells an
  experience and a philosophy first, data second.

## What works
- Proves a longevity/medical-wellness brand can read entirely as travel
  and hospitality — full-bleed nature/spa photography, restrained sans
  type, and near-absence of clinical UI (no charts, no biomarker grids on
  the homepage) — while still signaling medical seriousness through
  vocabulary ("psychoneuroimmunology," "chronomedicine") and awards.
- The powder-blue accent used at near-zero frequency keeps the whole site
  feeling calm rather than "branded."

## Avoid
- This register depends entirely on exceptional, consistent photography;
  without it the extreme restraint would read as an empty template.
- Because there's no dashboard/data on the homepage, this direction is a
  poor fit if biomarker/quantified-self content needs to be the hero.

## How to apply
- Use a single humanist sans at conservative sizes, an off-white plus
  slate-text base, and exactly one under-saturated accent hue reserved for
  CTAs/badges only — let full-bleed photography of real facilities and
  people (not stock, not renders) carry the "premium medical" signal
  instead of clinical UI chrome.
- Break a wordmark or headline across stacked lines at hero scale as a
  distinctive alternative to a single huge line of type.
- Reserve numeric/data presentation for a secondary page; keep the
  marketing homepage experiential rather than dashboard-like if the brand
  goal is "resort" over "health-tech."
